results.title: Steelers Cut Aaron Rodgers After QB Rips Mike McCarthy
results.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers waived Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday after the quarterback said on "The Pat McAfee Show" that he would not return to the team. Rodgers also alleged that coach Mike McCarthy has fallen asleep during team meetings. "That ship has sailed," said Rodgers of his time with the Steelers. Because the release came after the trade deadline, Rodgers is subject to waivers. He will become an unrestricted free agent if he goes unclaimed. Rodgers said he learned of his benching from tight end Pat Freiermuth, not McCarthy, despite long conversations with the coach over the previous two days. He described a quarterback meeting from last week. "Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring," said Rodgers. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened." Rodgers said McCarthy ended his halftime speech during Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles with "one, two, three, Packers." He also said McCarthy often had not watched game film by Tuesday and did not want to get to know the defense. Rodgers said he raised concerns with McCarthy on Monday and told him to release him if he was benched. He said the problems date to training camp. Rodgers said he vouched for McCarthy to general manager Omar Khan during last year's coaching search. Multiple league sources corroborated Rodgers' account to ESPN. Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, had said this would be his final season. Mason Rudolph will start Friday against the Denver Broncos.
